_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This is an executive summary of the policies, procedures and activities for compliance with the EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Requirements - Risk Management Program pursuant to Title 40 Part 68 of the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR 68) for LANXESS Solutions' (LANXESS) Bushy Park Site located in Goose Creek, SC. 

The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:
The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies are addressed in the individual RMP procedures which detail the RMP program requirements as well as how LANXESS complies with the applicable requirements. The Bushy Park facility is a nonresponding facility for releases of the RMP-listed chemicals.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:
Stationary Source:
The Bushy Park facility's primary activity is the manufacture of additives for the rubber industry. 

Regulated Substances Handled & Covered Process:
The LANXESS Bushy Park facility uses one chemical, that is subject to reporting under this filing to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The chemical is necessary to manufacture the additives at the Bushy Park facility. 

The regulated substance present at the Bushy Park facility is cyclohexylamine. Cyclohexylamine is regulated as a toxic substance. Cyclohexylamine is a colorless liquid with an ammonia-like odor. The LANXESS Bushy Park facility does not have any flammables that require inclusion in the Risk Management Plan. 

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:
The Bushy Park facility has implemented the Program Level 3 prevention program requirements under the RMP regulations. The required elements of the RMP prevention program are listed below:

Employee Participation
Process Safety Information
Process Hazard Analysis
Operating Procedures
Training
Contractors
Pre-startup Safety Review
Mechanical Integri

ty
Hot Work Permit
Management of Change
Incident Investigation
Compliance Audits

These items, their specific requirements, and how the LANXESS Bushy Park facility complies with the requirements are addressed in the individual procedural documents. In addition, the facility meets the requirements of the RMP Emergency Planning and Response element as detailed below.

The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:
The LANXESS Bushy Park facility has had zero RMP reportable incidents in the previous five years.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:
In the event of an incident or emergency, LANXESS has systems in place to respond quickly. Plant operators would ensure the plant is in a safe state and evacuate. Processes can be shut down on an emergency basis and the facility has a plan in place for evacuations, adequate first aid, and medical treatment and notification of local emergency response agencies. The facility is considered a non-responding facility. The Charleston International Manufacturing Complex (CIMC) has an emergency response team including Fire, Hazmat, Rescue, and Medical.  The CIMC emergency response procedures for the entire manufacturing complex are stored electronically in LANXESS' shared folder while LANXESS maintains site specific guidelines. Additionally, LANXESS would rely on the Berkeley Co. Emergency Preparedness for additional response to a chemical release.

As is customary with other companies at CIMC, LANXESS employees participate with CIMC in a number of ways: training, outreach, and the communication of incidents and items regarding regulatory compliance for all tenants.  Information is communicated through the Safety, Security and Pollution Prevention (S2P2) and Site Operations Council (SOC) groups made up of HSE professionals and site leadership, respectively. In addition, CIMC coordinates a Community Advisory Panel (CAP) discussion to address communication and information sharing with interested external parties thro

ugh a multi-jurisdictional / multi-organizational approach.  LANXESS regularly attends meetings held by the CAP and the Berkeley County Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC).  

Additionally, the LANXESS Bushy Park site trains operators on the safe handling of cyclohexylamine using a rigorous training program with in-depth studies of the manufacturing process (equipment and chemicals used, SDSs, etc) outlined in On-the-Job checklists.  Further, the Process Safety Information (PSI) document for the manufacturing process includes data on raw material hazards, locations of documents such as SDSs, P&IDs, work instructions, engineering files, safety interlock information, and raw material levels. LANXESS Healthy Safety Security Environmental Quality (HSSEQ), in conjunction with the corporate Production, Technology, Safety, and Environmental (PTSE) department, will address external requests for information related to cyclohexylamine releases or inquiries.

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:
The Bushy Park manufacturing facility has a continuing commitment to improve safety systems by implementing recommendations identified from Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) and compliance audits.
